internal.title: Incident Resolved: Checkout Service High Error Rate Due to Payment Error Injection
internal.body:
At 10:10 UTC, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service (47.5%). Initial diagnosis identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service, specifically related to the 'paymentFailure' flag causing invalid token errors during card charging attempts. The cart service was ruled out as a cause due to low error rates and no significant anomalies.

The remediation involved disabling the 'paymentFailure' flag at 10:30 UTC after approval. Post-remediation monitoring confirmed recovery with error rates returning to normal levels (below 0.5%).

Timeline:
- 10:10:39: Alert received for checkout service error rate spike.
- 10:30:22: Diagnosis confirmed payment error injection.
- 10:30:28: Flag disabled after approval.
- 10:30:28: Recovery verified with normalized error rates.

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issues
external.body: Between 10:10 and 10:30 UTC, some customers experienced failures completing checkout due to issues in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a problematic configuration flag. Normal service resumed shortly after, and we are monitoring to ensure continued stability. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.
